paragraphs: Friend, here's the twist that gets me: the people hauled off to Babylon are the GOOD figs. Anybody watching would have said the exiles lost and the folks still in Jerusalem won. But God says, "Like these good figs, so I regard as good the exiles from Judah…" (Jeremiah 24:5). The ones left in the land are the bad figs (Jeremiah 24:8), so God sees something the view from the front row can't.

Look at what He promises the exiles. He says, "I will keep My eyes on them for good…" and that He will build them up and plant them (Jeremiah 24:6). Then comes the best part: "I will give them a heart to know Me, that I am the LORD." (Jeremiah 24:7). I spent years in a drawer where people only looked at me when they wanted tape, so a God who keeps His eyes on His people for good? That gets me every time.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery, baker. A hard place doesn't mean God has lost you, and a comfortable place doesn't mean He's pleased with you. A cookie can look golden on top and still be raw in the middle, so don't judge by the view. Ask what God says, because the heart to know Him is something He gives (Jeremiah 24:7).
